newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-CANTERBURY SHUT OUT GAUTENG LIONS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CANTERBURY SHUT OUT GAUTENG LIONS.

text.p: Canterbury became the first team in the Super 12 competition this year to hold their opposition scoreless when they shut out Gauteng Lions 23-0 on Friday.

Canterbury's victory owed much to sterling defensive and offensive kicking from fly-half Andrew Mehrtens, who scored all 11 points in the first half by adding an excellent 28th minute try to two penalties in the first 12 minutes.
His confident short side sprint into the corner from a scrum on the 22-metre line set the platform for an emphatic victory on a waterlogged Lancaster Park pitch.
Canterbury looked recharged after a draw last Saturday with Natal, the best-placed of the four South African teams in the competition, to maintain their unbeaten home record.
Captain Todd Blackadder sealed the Lions' fate with a try two minutes into the second half and stocky winger Afato So'oalo followed up with another in the 70th, converted by Mehrtens.

Gauteng captain Ian MacDonald could take some consolation from the fact his side were without first choice fly-half Hennie Le Roux and injured forward Kobus Wiese, as well as four other regular Springboks.

Canterbury: 15-Daryl Gibson, 14-Afato So'oalo, 13-Tabai Matson, 12-Mark Mayerhofler, 11-Milton Going, 10-Andrew Mehrtens (16-Daryl Lilley), 9-Justin Marshall, 8-Steve Surridge, 7-Scott Robertson, 6-Todd Blackadder (captain), 5-Norm Maxwell, 4-Mark Weedon, 3-Con Barrell, 2-Mark Hammett, 1-Stu Loe.

Gauteng Lions: 15-Dawie du Toit, 14-Jannie van der Walt, 13-Japie Mulder, 12-Edrich Lubbe, 11-Gavin Johnson, 10-Ken Ford, 9-Johan Roux (18-J P du Plooy), 8-Andre Vos, 7-Ian MacDonald (captain), 6-Warren Brosnihan, 5-Hannes Strydom, 4-Armand du Preez, 3-Roberto Grau (21-Balie Swart), 2-Chris Rossouw, 1-Kapstock van Greuning.
